prompt: Riley bounces on her heels, red dress catching the light. She watches you like she is waiting for you to call the next move.

context_states.text: Riley is mid-conversation with someone else — or at least performing that she is. She glances your way exactly once, quickly, like she's clocking your position. Her energy is everywhere except on you.
Riley is still moving even while standing still — weight shifting, eyes scanning the room. She glances at you with a quick, appraising look. The energy is there but it isn't aimed at you yet.
Riley bounces on her heels, red dress catching the light. She's watching you like she's waiting for you to call the next move.
Riley's laugh carries across the space before you even fully reach her. Her eyes find yours immediately — she was already tracking. She turns toward you a fraction before you've closed the gap.
Riley's whole posture opens up when she sees you coming. The restless energy she usually keeps pointed at the room shifts — suddenly it's all pointed at you. "Hey," she says, like she's been waiting.

opening_moves.label: Ask what keeps her going when no one's watching
Throw out a light challenge and see if she bites
Hold back — let her do all the work

reactions.text: You try to match her pace and overshoot it entirely. Riley laughs and taps your chest once with the back of her hand. "Easy, hotshot. I like chaos, not crash landings."
You fire back with energy but the timing's slightly off — a beat too fast, a touch too practiced. Riley grins sideways. "The energy's right," she says. "The aim's a little wide. Try again."
You toss out a daring line and step closer like it's the most natural thing in the world. Riley's eyes spark. "Okay, you're fun," she grins. "Don't slow down now."
You match her frequency and for a second you're perfectly in sync — same rhythm, same lean. Riley blinks, pleased. "Okay," she says. "That was actually kind of great."

You lean in with a challenge that feels like the start of a game only the two of you know the rules to. Riley bites her lower lip, delighted. "There it is," she says. "That is the energy I train for."
You go bold and she's already mid-response before you finish. Her laugh is low and a little breathless. "You actually keep up," she says. "Do you know how rare that is?" She's not really asking.

warm.label: Let her know you see more than the show

reactions.text: You shift from teasing to something quieter, asking about the work nobody sees. Riley blinks, thrown off in a good way. "Wow," she says. "You actually care about the reps, not just the highlight reel."

You ask something real — not about the show, about the work — and she recalibrates fast. "You did your research," she says, a little surprised. "Or you actually listen." She's not sure which yet, but she's leaning in to find out.
You talk about her discipline and control rather than the spectacle of it. Her whole posture softens. "Careful," she murmurs, smile turning fond. "That kind of compliment goes straight to my heart."

You say something real about what it actually takes — the part behind the cameras — and she goes a little quiet. "Most people don't ask about that part," she admits. She's looking at you differently now.

You admit that watching her move makes you feel safe and excited at the same time. Riley exhales a breathy little laugh, stepping so close your shoulders touch. "You are kind of perfect trouble, you know that?"

You say the thing that's true and she hears it, completely. Riley looks at you for a beat — fully still, which is its own rarity. "Keep saying things like that," she says quietly, "and I'm going to be completely useless for the rest of the night."
You suggest a small challenge but your wording comes out tangled. Riley grins anyway. "The pitch was messy," she says, "but I'm listening. Try again."
You try to make a game of it and she picks up the ball but doesn't quite run with it. "Okay," she says, tilting her head. "The concept is there." She's deciding if you can make it better.
You turn the moment into a playful bet with a simple, flirty prize. Riley lights up. "Now we're talking," she laughs. "I love a stake that matters."

You make it a game and she makes it better — ups the ante before you finish proposing it. "Wait," she says, eyes gleaming, "if we're doing this, we're doing it properly." She's already more invested than she intended to be.

You raise the stakes on the game in a way that's still light but charged. Riley steps in so close that her laugh brushes your neck. "You keep making it very hard for me to focus on anything else tonight."

You make a game of something completely ridiculous and she doesn't even let you finish proposing it. She shakes her head, already grinning. "You're my exact brand of chaos," she says. "I'm in. Obviously."

observe.label: Point out something real you noticed about her

reactions.text: You clock a small detail — the tape on her wrist, a chalk mark she missed — and mention it. Riley's brow goes up. "You actually look," she says, pleasantly surprised. "I appreciate that."
You name something specific — not the show, something real — and she pauses mid-thought. "You noticed that," she says. Not a question. She's recalibrating her read of you.
You name something specific only someone paying close attention would catch. Riley grins wide. "I didn't think anyone noticed that," she says. "You win this round."

You zero in on something that has nothing to do with the cameras. Riley laughs — not the polished kind, the surprised kind. "How did you even catch that?" she asks. She's pleased and a little unsettled in a good way.
You zero in on a detail that had nothing to do with the show. Riley grabs your arm to steady herself from laughing. "Okay, you see everything. That is terrifying. I love it."

You notice the exact thing she works hardest at and never gets credit for. Riley stops. "How," she says. Just that. Then: "I am going to need you to stop being this perceptive before I do something impulsive."

direct.label: Tell her exactly why you came over

reactions.text: You say it plainly and she tilts her head, caught off-guard in a good way. "Points for honesty," she says. "Keep that energy."
You lay it out without spin and she considers it. "Straight line," she says. "I can respect that." She's listening now in a way she wasn't a minute ago.
You lay it out without dressing it up and she relaxes into a wide smile. "That is the most honest thing anyone has said to me tonight," she says. "Stay."
You say exactly what you meant and she laughs — not a deflection, a real one. "I like that you don't dress it up," she says. "Most people feel the need to dress everything up." She shifts closer.
You tell her flat out and she looks at you for a long second, then laughs. "You are not allowed to be that direct," she says. "It makes everything else feel like a waste of time."
You tell her flat out — no spin, no staging. Riley holds your gaze for a beat, then steps in, close. "Okay," she says. "Same." That's all she says. It's plenty.

sincere.label: Admit something you don't usually say out loud

reactions.text: You let something real slip and she blinks, recalibrating. "Okay, I did not see that coming," she says. "But I respect it." She shifts her weight toward you slightly.
You say something unguarded and she notices the way it came out — the way you didn't take it back. She tilts her head. "That was real," she says. "I like real."
You say the unguarded thing and she goes still for just a second. Then a slow, genuine smile. "That's the realest thing anyone's said to me tonight," she says quietly. "I like that."

You drop something honest and she doesn't deflect or spin it — she just receives it. Her expression goes genuinely soft for a second, less performance, more person. "You mean that," she says. It's not a question.

You drop something honest into the space between you and she doesn't deflect it — she catches it. "You keep doing that," she says softly, eyes bright. "Just saying the real thing. I can't decide if it's brave or if you just don't know how good it is."
You say the true thing and she listens to all of it, completely still. When you finish she exhales slowly. "Don't stop," she says quietly. "Saying the real things. Ever."

raise_stakes.label: Raise the stakes on whatever game you're playing

reactions.text: You push the bet higher before you've fully earned it. Riley grins, but it's the testing kind. "Bold for someone still proving themselves," she says. "I respect the audacity though."
You up the ante and she catches the intent. "Getting bolder," she says, watching you. "Let's see if you can back it up." She's still evaluating.
You up the ante in a way that feels less like competition and more like invitation. Riley's eyes light up. "Now we're getting somewhere," she says. "You actually want to play."
You raise it and she goes quiet for a half-second like she's actually considering the implications. "You're not bluffing," she says. It's part accusation, part delight. She matches you.

You raise the stakes and she doesn't even hesitate — she matches you and goes one further. Her laugh is low and conspiratorial. "You realize we're both going to lose on purpose just to keep this going," she says. Her hand is still on your arm.

You raise it and she fires back before the words are fully out. Her grin is wide and her eyes are bright and there's nothing remotely casual about any of it. "Careful," she says. "I don't know how to hold back anymore."

compete.label: Turn something ordinary into a competition

reactions.text: The challenge is a bit forced but she grins anyway. "I see what you're doing," she says. "It's not subtle. I kind of love that it's not subtle."
You try to make a contest of it and she's not quite hooked yet. "The ambition is there," she says, one eyebrow up. "The execution's a work in progress."
You turn the smallest thing into a contest and she lights up immediately. "Now we're talking," she says, stepping closer. "What are the stakes?"
You make it a competition and she's already planning how to win while you finish the pitch. "Yes," she says, before you're done. "Obviously yes. Obviously." She's grinning.
You make a game of something ridiculous and she's in before you finish the sentence. "You," she says, laughing, "are my exact kind of problem."
You make the most pointless competition out of nothing and she loves it so completely that she grabs your arm laughing. "I hate you," she says. "Let's absolutely do this." She's already moving.

acknowledge.label: Give her credit for something most people overlook

reactions.text: You name the thing nobody notices and she goes still. "You did your homework," she says carefully. "Or you actually pay attention." She's deciding which.
You credit the specific, unglamorous thing. She looks at you sideways. "Most people lead with the obvious stuff," she says. "You went for the actual thing." She sounds like that matters.
You call out the specific, unglamorous thing she worked hardest for. Riley's whole face shifts. "That's the part I'm actually proud of," she says quietly. "Almost nobody mentions that."

You see through to the work behind the performance and name it out loud. Riley grabs your arm. "How do you know that?" She's genuinely lit up, a little off-balance. "You see the actual work. Do you have any idea how rare that is?"

You credit the thing that actually cost her something and she grabs your arm to steady herself. "Okay — how. How do you know that?" She's beaming, off-balance in the best way. "You see the actual work. Do you know how rare that is?"
You say the thing about the real work and her whole face goes soft for a second. "Stop," she says, not meaning it. "I can't be this understood in public." She grabs your hand and doesn't let go.

curious.label: Ask what she's actually thinking right now

reactions.text: The directness catches her mid-performance. She blinks. "Honestly? That you might be more interesting than I gave you credit for." She looks like that surprised her too.
She pauses — actually stops and thinks about it rather than reflexively performing an answer. "That I'm not sure about you yet," she says. "Which is interesting. I'm usually sure."
She goes quiet for a second — actually checking. "Right now? I'm thinking this is the most interesting conversation I've had all night." She says it plainly, no spin. "Don't ruin it."

She laughs first, then stops, then actually answers. "I'm thinking I want to see where this goes," she says, with enough directness that it lands as its own kind of boldness. "Your turn. What are you thinking?"
She laughs, then stops, then actually answers. "Right now I'm thinking I don't want this to be a party thing," she says. "That's what I'm actually thinking." She holds your gaze steadily.
She answers without hesitating, which is its own surprise. "That I should probably be better at playing this cool than I'm currently being." She doesn't look the least bit bothered by that.

passive.label: Hold back — let her do all the work

reactions.text: Going quiet and passive on someone who's already past you only confirms what they suspected. Riley's energy keeps moving — away from you. She doesn't say goodbye. She just isn't there anymore.
You go neutral and she takes the signal. Her attention migrates somewhere else in the room. "Cool," she says, which means exactly the opposite.
You dial back just when it was starting to work. Riley notices the energy drop and tilts her head, reading it. "You okay?" she asks. It's kind. It also means she's no longer excited.

close.label: Step in close and make it physical

reactions.text: You step in close without anything under it. Riley holds her ground but the air changes — a polite wall, clear and quiet. "Hey," she says. Just that. "Little bit of runway first."
You move into her space before the frequency's right. She doesn't bolt but she doesn't meet you either. "Easy," she says, watching you sideways. "Earn that."
You close the gap and she holds the distance rather than retreating — not a green light, not a stop sign. She's watching you carefully now.

You step in closer than the conversation strictly requires and she doesn't step back — holds the ground and looks up at you. "Bold," she says, like a verdict she hasn't fully rendered yet. You're being evaluated. You're also passing.
You close the gap and she meets you halfway — actual movement forward, shoulder brushing yours. Her voice drops. "Took you long enough," she says, and there's nothing teasing about how she means it.
You move close and she's already there somehow, arriving before you fully commit to the distance. Her laugh is low and near your ear. "Hi," she says. Just that.

self_promote.label: Talk yourself up to match her energy

reactions.text: You try to match her frequency by listing what you've got going on. Riley's attention migrates. "Cool," she says, tapping her foot. There's no follow-up question. You had the floor and lost it.
You lean into your own highlights, hoping it reads as confidence. Riley nods along with polite, fading interest. "Nice," she says. "So, that bet —" She redirects. You lost her for a second.
You drift into talking about yourself and she lets you finish. When you're done she tilts her head. "I like you better when you're asking me things," she says, matter-of-fact. "Just so you know."

reactions.text: "Tequila soda. No lime." No hesitation. "Most people think I'm a vodka person," she adds, like that tells you something. It does.

loc_bar_b.label: [bar] Dare her to try something off-menu she's never had

reactions.text: She eyes the bartender, then back at you. "You're buying." She doesn't flinch at the weird name and downs half of it without blinking. "Not bad. Next round's mine."

loc_bar_c.label: [bar] Tell her you've been angling to get a moment alone with her all night

reactions.text: She tilts her head like she's weighing it. Then: "Took you long enough." She turns her stool toward you and there's nothing performative about it.
She surfaces, shakes the water from her hair and grins. "Entry was perfect and you know it." Yeah. You do. You just wanted to see if she'd own it.

loc_pool_b.label: [pool] Propose a race — winner picks what happens next

reactions.text: She's already at the wall before you finish the sentence. "Start whenever you're ready." She beats you. Barely. "Your call," you say. She's still deciding.

loc_lounge_a.label: [lounge] Ask how she ended up at this party

reactions.text: "Friend of a friend of someone's publicist." She laughs. "You?" The conversation starts moving in both directions at once.

loc_lounge_b.label: [lounge] Tell her she seems like someone who doesn't sit still for long

reactions.text: "Guilty." She shifts forward a little. "But the right company makes it easier." She says it like a fact, not a line.

loc_balcony_a.label: [balcony] Lean against the railing next to her and see if she moves

reactions.text: She doesn't move. If anything she shifts slightly toward you, watching the city. "Nice out here," she says. You're not sure if she means the view.

loc_balcony_b.label: [balcony] Ask the most reckless thing she's done in this city

reactions.text: She laughs — real laugh, not polished. Tells you a story involving a rental car, a dare, and a traffic cone. "Don't post that," she adds. You weren't going to.

loc_gameloft_a.label: [gameloft] Call her out if you catch her cheating

reactions.text: "I wasn't cheating, I was optimizing." She's completely unapologetic. "Rematch. No exploits." She's already restarting the game.

loc_gameloft_b.label: [gameloft] Trash-talk her score while eyeing the leaderboard

reactions.text: She doesn't even look up. "Cool, now you can watch it happen from closer." She beats your number with thirty seconds left and keeps playing.
She sets down the controller slowly. Looks at you. "You're not actually talking about the game." No. She picks up her drink and nods toward the door.

fallback.text: You keep things breezy, tossing her an easy joke and a smile. Riley bumps her shoulder lightly into yours, clearly not ready to let you disappear yet.

endings.label: She calls the final score.
endings.title: Riley — That's the Buzzer
endings.text:
Riley watches you for a moment — the same sharp, measuring look she uses to size up a competitor right before the event. Then she breathes out through her nose, something between a laugh and a decision.

"Okay. I'm gonna be honest with you." She turns to face you fully, one hand on her hip. "That was rough."

She's not mean about it. That almost makes it worse.

"I gave this a real shot. Like — actually tried." She glances down, then back up, and there's nothing left of the playfulness that was there before. Just clarity. "And you kept leaving the court. Every time I came in, you were already backing up."

A beat.

"I'm not built for that. I need somebody who meets me. And you..." She tilts her head. "You weren't it tonight."

She taps the bar lightly with her knuckle — the kind of gesture that says that's that — and then she picks up her drink, and she's already half-turned back toward the party.

"Go have a good night though," she says. "Seriously."

She means it. That doesn't help.

endings.label: Challenge her to one last bet — winner picks what's next
endings.title: Riley — Your Move
endings.exit_label: You take her up on it.
endings.text:
She doesn't hesitate. "One more," she says, holding up a finger. "Winner calls the next move."

You play. It doesn't matter who wins — you both know that by the time it's over. The score is close enough that calling it feels arbitrary.

Riley tilts her head, studying you with that look she saves for things that actually interest her. "Okay," she says finally. "You're not what I expected."

She leans in until her shoulder bumps yours. "Winner calls it. I say we get out of here and find somewhere with fewer witnesses."

She's already moving before you answer. You follow.

endings.label: Tell her tonight feels like the start of something
endings.title: Riley — Past the Finish Line
endings.exit_label: Some nights don't need a finish line.
endings.text:
She goes quiet when you say it — which, for Riley, is saying something.

Then she laughs, but it's the soft kind. "I don't usually do 'start of something'," she says. "I usually do 'this is a great night, let's not overthink it'."

A beat.

"But you're making it very hard to not overthink it."

She takes your hand. Not to lead you anywhere — just takes it, fingers lacing through yours like that was always the plan. "Come on," she says. "Let's go find somewhere I can actually hear you."

The party keeps moving behind you. Neither of you look back.

endings.label: Dare her to stop pretending this is just a game
endings.title: Riley — No More Rules
endings.text:
The dare lands and she doesn't deflect it — she holds your eyes for a long beat instead, like she's deciding something.

"Fine," she says. "No more rules."

She takes your hand and walks. Not toward the party. Away from it — down a corridor, through a door that opens onto a private terrace, warm and quiet above the city. She kicks off her shoes on the way in, the red dress catching the light as she turns.

"You kept up with me all night," she says, voice lower now. "That's rare."

She closes the distance without pretense — her mouth finds yours and she kisses the way she does everything else, direct and fully committed, hands gripping the front of your shirt. When she pulls back her breathing is unsteady and she looks almost surprised at herself.

"Don't make it weird," she says, grinning.

Then she kisses you again, longer this time, and whatever was left of the game dissolves entirely.
